text:
mia: Quick heads-up — HF->Redwood conversion for `nano-chat-7b` surfaced a normalization/whitespace mismatch during quant eval. token counts up by +2 in some chat cases.

raj: Can you paste a minimal repro? is this NFC vs NFKC or byte-fallback?

mia: Repro below. HF tokenizer (from model repo) nibble: `tokenizer.normalizer` is set to `NFKC`, but our fallback path in converter left it unset so Redwood runtime used NFC semantics.

mia: HF run:
```
>>> tokenizer.normalize("\u00A0hi")  # non-breaking space + hi
'\u00A0hi'  # NFKC keeps NBSP here in this model's config (weird)
>>> tokenizer.encode("  hi")
[50256, 16]  # counts = 2 tokens in HF baseline
```

mia: Converted -> Redwood runtime tokenization:
```
>>> redwood_tokenize("  hi")
[50256, 16, 0]  # extra pad / bytefallback-ish token seen in some runs
```

lisa: That extra 0 looks like a special token got injected — maybe `pad_token` mapping. Did converter rewrite `config.json` special_tokens_map?

mia: I checked — converter copies `config.json` but we didn't propagate `special_tokens_map` consistently when `add_prefix_space: true` is implied by chat template. Some HF chat templates assume leading-space normalization.

ethan: Related: during quant runs (int8), we saw measurably different LM-loss on the eval set for examples that start with whitespace. Could be cumulative from token mismatch.

raj: How widespread? single example or entire eval skew? numbers?

mia: Quick numbers from yesterday's bench: 1k chat turns, whitespace-leading examples ~8% of dataset. Tokenization mismatch accounted for ~18% of loss delta on that slice (huge). Global avg loss delta smaller but detectable.

lisa: Sounds like two fixes: 1) make converter propagate normalizer config exactly (NFKC vs NFC) and `add_prefix_space`/`prefix_tokens` flags; 2) ensure special_tokens_map -> runtime mapping preserved (pad/unk/eos ids).

ethan: Also check byte-fallback order. Some HF tokenizers use bytefallback to handle isolated control bytes. If converter changes fallback table ordering, rare unicode sequences can map to different token ids.

mia: Agreed. I have a small patch in a branch that: copies `tokenizer.json` normalizer field verbatim, copies `special_tokens_map` and uses HF's `added_tokens` roundtrip. It also adds a test: token-roundtrip for a list of edgecases (NBSP, ZWJ, combining marks, leading double-space).

mia: Patch gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/sample-token-fix (quick link)

ci-bot: CI: added token-roundtrip test triggered. Running quant bench with new converter. ETA ~45m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

raj: Good. Once CI passes, run a canary quant of the model and compare per-slice LM loss (whitespace slice + non-ascii slice). If small regressions remain, we can try enabling a conservative `preserve_whitespace` flag on Redwood runtime for this model.

lisa: One more gotcha — chat template wrappers often add `\n` or leading spaces for assistant prompts. If HF template used `\nAssistant: ` but converter stripped the space, you'll get consistent off-by-one tokens in every turn. Repro that too.

mia: Yep that was in our failing eval set — some templates had leading space in `system`+`assistant` few-shot strings. I added template roundtrip tests as well.

ethan: Nice. Can we add a lightweight fuzz of 200 random unicode sequences to the roundtrip tests? might expose more bytefallback ordering issues before quant runs.

mia: Will add. For now CI shows token test pass locally. I'll push patch and follow-up with the canary quant results.

raj: Thanks — please post the canary metrics (per-slice loss and token-delta histogram). If we still see >0.5% unit-cost impact from token growth we lock the model from auto-quant and require manual signoff.

mia: Will do. Thanks all. :slightly_smiling_face:
